title: The Key to Safe Scripting & Automation

scenes.line2: How do you keep prod safe?
scenes.say: What's the single most important rule for scripting and automation? How do you make sure your scripts don't break production?

scenes.label: Idempotent
scenes.sub: Scripts must be safe to run over and over.
scenes.say: The answer: idempotency. Your scripts must be safe to run again and again, with the same result every time.
Here’s how: Check before you change. Add a dry-run mode. Exit on any failure. And always log what your script does.
In Bash, you parse text and check exit codes. In PowerShell, you filter objects directly, which is safer and less error-prone.

scenes.title: Real-World Tools
scenes.say: For real-world automation, use jq to safely parse JSON, and Ansible to run checks or changes across many servers at once.

scenes.question: How do you avoid breaking prod?
scenes.right: Add idempotency, dry-run, strict errors, logging, review, and staged rollout.
scenes.say: Here's a classic trap: Just testing on dev isn't enough. In interviews, mention idempotency, dry-run, error handling, logging, and rolling out changes in stages.
